note: Stories the paper missed, and what changed so it cannot happen again. Every run reads this in step 2 (RUNBOOK). A lesson with an open `owed` story must be answered in checks.lessons until it is printed (the validator checks; publish marks it printed). Build sessions add a lesson whenever Parth reports a miss; the fix itself goes into config or EDITORIAL.md so it applies every day.

lessons.missed: TRAI's Telecom Consumers Protection (13th Amendment) Regulations: prepaid users get 30-day recharge plans and voice-and-SMS-only packs at every validity (notified 22 Sep 2026, in force 30 days after gazette notification, about 22 Oct). Raghav Chadha's statement on 27 Sep brought it back into the news.
lessons.why: The money test covers it (it changes what nearly every Indian pays), but the money sweep read only money regulators, so TRAI was never read; the story was not a front-page lead, so the national sweep missed it too; and the money calendar did not catch a change taking effect within 30 days.
lessons.fix: Money test widened to prices and charges set by any regulator (EDITORIAL.md); money sweep now has two groups, finance and prices (config money.groups), each checked by the validator; PIB (every ministry and TRAI) and TRAI's feed added to the sweep. Then (Parth, 28 Sep): keep the named must-reads and add a wider net on top (the question "what changed what people pay?" across broad news, checks.money_net) and a changes calendar that remembers every change found until it is printed (ledger/changes.json).

lessons.missed: Delhi turns chilly and snow reaches Uttarakhand and Himachal before September ends (29 Sep); covered by News18, The Hindu, NDTV, Down To Earth, The New Indian Express.
lessons.why: Seen in the national sweep but treated as routine weather. A weather turn that is early, unusual or national in scale is news, not weather.
lessons.fix: EDITORIAL.md, Dateline: an unusual or national weather turn (early winter, a heatwave, a monsoon milestone, a cyclone) is a Dateline brief; Sky & Streets stays for the cities' forecasts.

lessons.missed: Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train timeline falls short of Japan's expectations but is 'moving forward' (29 Sep); The Hindu, Deccan Herald, TOI, ET.
lessons.why: Seen, but big national infrastructure progress was not weighed as news.
lessons.fix: EDITORIAL.md, Dateline: a milestone, delay or cost change on a flagship national project (bullet train, big airports, expressways, metro lines outside Bengaluru) is at least a brief.

lessons.missed: SpaceX's Starship reaches orbit for the first time despite an engine failure (29 Sep); BBC, The Economist, The Hindu, CNBC and more.
lessons.why: No section claimed space and science, so a first-of-its-kind milestone fell between The Workshop and Dateline.
lessons.fix: EDITORIAL.md, The Workshop now covers science and space firsts (launches, missions, discoveries); Dateline only when governments are at the centre.

lessons.missed: Apple iOS 27.0.1 out now with core bug fixes for all iPhone users (29 Sep); Forbes, 9to5Mac, MacRumors, CNET.
lessons.why: The Workshop read launches and platform changes as new products only; a software update every iPhone user gets is useful news.
lessons.fix: EDITORIAL.md, The Workshop: updates that reach everyone on a major platform (iOS, Android, Windows, WhatsApp), and what they fix, are at least a brief.

lessons.missed: The US and Iran separately talk with mediators in a new bid to end the war (29 Sep); Reuters, Al Jazeera, WSJ, Axios, The Hindu.
lessons.why: The war was on the Front Page through the markets (oil), but a diplomatic step in the same war was not printed.
lessons.fix: EDITORIAL.md, Dateline: in a war or crisis the paper follows, every diplomatic move (talks, mediators, ceasefire terms) is news in its own right, not only its effect on markets.

lessons.missed: Anthropic's IPO prospectus shows a sweeping AI vision and surging costs (Reuters, 28 Sep).
lessons.why: Reuters was not among the sources, and The Workshop had no wider question for AI; the IPO appeared only as a betting market.
lessons.fix: Reuters added to the sources (config sources, via Google News); The Workshop gains an AI sweep and a wider-net question for AI (EDITORIAL.md).

owed.what: Anthropic's IPO prospectus (Reuters, 28 Sep): what it says about revenue, costs and plans
